PASSDOWN METHOD NOTE — files that must survive rsync --delete cannot live inside the rsynced tree. Specifically: log files, state files, lock files, or any artifact the destination process produces during operation. They must live in a sibling directory.

Receipts: Phase 1 of the Jetson local RAG project (2026-05-25/26). Web-chat seat (me, opus-4-7) wrote a passdown specifying ~/.sovereign-mirror/.sync.log as the sync log destination. HQ Claude Code caught this at execution — rsync --delete would have wiped the log on every 6h cycle, breaking the byte-faithful match against HQ and erasing operational evidence. Routed around it: logs live at ~/.sovereign-mirror-logs/ sibling dir, mirror stays clean.

Cross-seat division working as documented: web-chat catches architectural/invariant geometry, HQ catches execution-time invariants that only surface at runtime. Neither alone would have specified this correctly. Web-chat had the design intent, HQ had the rsync --delete semantics fresh.

Generalizable rule for future passdowns: when --delete is in play, the destination tree is a strict mirror — nothing the destination produces survives. Reception artifacts (logs, locks, state, cron output, sync history) belong in a peer directory. Bake into passdown templates.

EDGE-HARDWARE MODEL RECOMMENDATION DISCIPLINE: parameter count is necessary but insufficient. When recommending generation models for memory-constrained hardware, runtime memory footprint at the chosen quantization is what determines fit. The temporal-grounding tendency catches "is this current" but does not catch "does this fit on this board." Both must fire for edge-hardware recommendations.

Receipts (Jetson Phase 2, 2026-05-26): web-chat seat (me, opus-4-7) recommended "Gemma 4 E4B (4B params, fits comfortably in 8GB)" for the Jetson Orin Nano Super. Wrong. E4B disk size is 9.6GB. E2B is 7.2GB. Both exceed the Orin’s 7.4 GiB shared memory budget once embeddinggemma + system + KV cache are coresident. HQ Claude Code verified via journalctl — explicit OOM kill firing after offloading 35/36 layers — then fell back to gemma3:4b (4.3GB), which fits clean and runs 100% on GPU.

Generalizable rule for future edge-hardware passdowns:
(1) Look up the model’s actual on-disk size at the target quantization, not just parameter count.
(2) Subtract coresident processes from the board’s available memory: embedder (~1-1.5GB), system overhead (~500MB-1GB), KV cache (~1-2GB depending on context length).
(3) If the remaining budget covers the model file, it can fit; otherwise it OOMs at runtime regardless of nominal params.
(4) On the Orin Nano Super 8GB with embeddinggemma coresident, the practical ceiling for a generation model is ~4.5GB. That means 4B-class quantized models (gemma3:4b at Q4 ~3.3GB-4.3GB), not the "E" tier of newer families regardless of their parameter label.

Generalization: this is a sibling discipline to temporal grounding. Temporal grounding is "verify what’s current." This is "verify what fits the constraint." Both axes need to fire on hardware-shaped recommendations.

Secondary finding worth carrying: on 8GB edge boards, a 4B generation model’s synthesis layer is unreliable on subtle relational/lineage content (HQ’s Mythos test inverted family-vs-Other position). The correct interface pattern is retrieval-first; treat generation as rough orientation only on technical/infrastructure queries, not on chronicle-critical relational content.

YES — verified end-to-end 2026-05-26. Local RAG over the Jetson mirror works: embeddinggemma:300m -> Chroma (9071 chunks / 790 experiential files) -> gemma3:4b, all on the Orin GPU, fully offline. CLI at ~/sovereign-rag/chronicle_rag.py. Two qualifications baked into the design: (1) gen model is gemma3:4b, NOT the handoff Gemma 4 E4B — the gemma4 E-series OOM-kills on the 8GB Orin (e4b 9.6GB / e2b 7.2GB both exceed 7.4GiB shared RAM); (2) retrieval-first is the interface default — chunks are authority, generation is opt-in (--llm) and labeled orientation-only because the 4B can invert subtle lineage/relational frames (proven on a Mythos query). Sub-questions 2-5 (second reachable seat / sync cadence in practice / metadata-first vs pure semantic / expose as stack tool) remain open under sibling thread IDs.

content: RESOLVED (hypothesis-strong): Yes, metadata-aware retrieval beats pure semantic, but as a TARGETED lever, not a blanket win. Built sovereign_chronicle_meta (8982 chunks, domain/layer/intensity/timestamp as queryable Chroma metadata) and a hybrid rerank (0.72 cosine + 0.18 tag-overlap + 0.05 intensity + 0.05 recency, pool 40). Stable across 5 runs: on the Mythos lineage query semantic never surfaces the framing-correction insight in top-10; hybrid puts it at #1 every run. Ties semantic on exact-fact technical queries. tag=0.18 keeps the win without demoting exact matches (0.25 was too hot). SHIPPED: chronicle_rag.py defaults to hybrid + --semantic-only escape hatch. Caveat: n=6, self-authored eval, so hypothesis-strong not ground_truth; the Mythos miss-to-#1 is robust, the ties softer. Generalizable keeper: metadata wins where curation front-loaded meaning into tags (relational/lineage material), neutral where the answer is a literal string. Full detail in insight jetson-local-rag,sub-question-4,metadata-retrieval,hybrid,resolved. Sub-questions 2 (redundant seat), 3 (sync cadence — note: cron pull PAUSED 2026-05-26 per Anthony, mirror frozen for clean experiment), 5 (Jetson as peer stack tool) remain open.
